text:
### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, the group A15, A16, A17, A19, A20 always ran before the group A14, A18, A21, A22, A23 whenever both occurred: A15 preceded A24 in 100 in 100 traces, and A15 preceded A22 in all of the roughly 23 in 100 traces containing both. In the later window, every such relation is inverted: A24 preceded A15 in 100 in 100 traces, and A22 preceded A15 in about 25 in 100. [REL004, REL002, REL020, REL028]

- Event positions moved accordingly. In the earlier window, A15/A16/A17/A19/A20 sat at about 39–40% of the trace length and A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 at about 69–71%; in the later window, the first group sits at about 64% and the second at about 32–35%. The connectors A24 (about 49% to 37%) and A28 (about 67% to 55%) also moved earlier, keeping A24 before A28. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS001, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]

- Successors flipped with the reversal. In the earlier window, A14, A18, A21, A22 and A23 led exclusively to A29 (for A14, all outgoing transitions, seen in 34 traces), while A15–A20 still sent roughly 16–29% of their outgoing transitions to A24. In the later window, the first group leads exclusively to A24, the transitions from A15–A20 to A24 disappeared, and about 18–22% of them now go to A29; A28 now leads entirely into A15/A16/A17/A19/A20 instead of A14/A18/A21/A22/A23, and A39 the other way round. [DIR001, DIR005, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, DIR012]

- Participation barely moved, so the difference is one of ordering rather than presence: A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 appear in every trace in both windows, and A14, A18, A21, A22, A23 in roughly 17–23 in 100 traces in both windows. [POS002, POS001, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two phases of the process exchanged their order: the block A14, A18, A21, A22, A23, previously executed in the later part of each trace after the block A15, A16, A17, A19, A20, is now executed early, before that block, while the connecting activities kept their middle positions but attached to the opposite blocks — A24 and A28 still run between the two blocks in the same relative order, but A24 now follows the early block and precedes the late one, A28 now leads into A15/A16/A17/A19/A20, A39 now leads into A14/A18/A21/A22/A23, and the observed transitions into A29 now come from A15/A16/A17/A19/A20 instead of from A14/A18/A21/A22/A23. [REL004, REL005, REL018, REL019, REL028, REL029, DIR001, DIR011, DIR012, POS001, POS002]

Supporting signs: all 31 relation items show the same complete flip with no mixed orders inside either window; the successor and position items agree in direction; participation of every involved activity is stable, so activities were neither added, removed nor made optional; and 55 items qualified against roughly 0.58 expected by chance in an unchanged process, far beyond what random re-splitting produces. [REL004, REL009, REL016, REL022, DIR002, DIR011, POS003, screening]

Limitations: positions are event-based rather than clock-based, and the block-to-block reversal is directly observed only in the roughly one in five traces containing the A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 activities (the A24 relation is observed in all traces); the evidence also cannot rule out that the two windows capture a flip in the mix of two long-standing orderings rather than a single modification. [REL002, REL004, POS001]

Other differences: none — all 55 qualified items describe the same reordering, and participation shares changed only marginally (for example, A22 appears in about 23 in 100 traces before and about 25 in 100 after). [POS009, DIR009]
